title: Cosimplicial frames compute localized mapping spaces
statement:
A model category here is a complete and cocomplete category with classes $C,F,W$ of cofibrations, fibrations and weak equivalences; $W$ satisfies two-out-of-three and is retract closed, and $(C,F\cap W)$ and $(C\cap W,F)$ are weak factorization systems with functorial factorizations. A weak factorization system means factorization of every morphism and the two mutually characterized diagonal-lifting classes. Trivial means also in $W$. An object is cofibrant when its initial map is in $C$, and fibrant when its terminal map is in $F$. Write $q_{\mathcal M}:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M_\infty=\mathcal M[W^{-1}]_\infty$ for homotopy coherent localization, universal for inverting $W$ including mapping spaces and composition homotopies. Infinity categories are modeled by simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] with fillers for all inner horns (the union of all faces of a standard simplex except a face other than the first or last). All required universes may be enlarged.

For a cofibrant object $X$ of any such $\mathcal M$, a cosimplicial frame is a functor $X^\bullet:\Delta\to\mathcal M$ with $X^0=X$, an augmentation $X^\bullet\to\operatorname{const}X$ that is an objectwise weak equivalence and whose degree-zero component is the identity of $X$, and cofibrations $L_nX^\bullet\to X^n$ for all $n$. Here $\Delta$ has finite nonempty ordered sets and order-preserving maps, and $L_n$ is the colimit over nonidentity injective maps $[k]\hookrightarrow[n]$. Such frames exist. Every object of $\mathcal M_\infty$ is equivalent to the image of a cofibrant object and to the image of a fibrant object. For every fibrant $Y$, the simplicial set $H(X^\bullet,Y)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(X^n,Y)$ is Kan and represents $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal M_\infty}(qX,qY)$, naturally in the homotopy theory of both inputs. A Kan complex means a simplicial set in which every horn has a filler. Every component of this mapping space is represented by an actual map $X\to Y$. If $p:Y\to Z$ is a fibration between fibrant objects, $H(X^\bullet,p)$ is a Kan fibration, trivial if $p$ is trivial. A Kan fibration means a map with the right lifting property for every horn inclusion. A strict pullback of Kan complexes along a Kan fibration represents their homotopy pullback, and finite products of these Kan fibrations are Kan fibrations. If $T:\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$ is the left adjoint of an adjunction and preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations, then $T$ preserves weak equivalences between cofibrant objects, $TX^\bullet$ is a frame on $TX$, and these mapping-space identifications are compatible with the functor induced by $T$ on cofibrant objects and by localization. In particular they identify evaluation and restriction maps whenever those are left Quillen functors. No simplicial enrichment, properness or combinatorial hypothesis is required.

source.place: Hovey Definition 5.2.7, Theorem 5.2.8, Corollary 5.4.4 and Proposition 5.4.7 (frames and Kan mapping complexes); Lemma 1.1.12 (Brown). Hinich, Dwyer-Kan localization revisited, arXiv:1311.4128v4, Proposition 1.2.1 and Theorem 1.3.3 (= Dwyer-Kan, Function complexes in homotopical algebra, 4.4), for identification with the universal infinity localization. Cisinski, Higher Categories and Homotopical Algebra, Corollary 3.8.4 and its proof, printed pp. 123-124, give the strict-pullback computation along a Kan fibration; finite products preserve Kan fibrations by componentwise horn lifting. No Stacks tag states the localization comparison.
